summary: Identity-proxy header reordering causes CLI SSO assertion mismatch and login loops
description: Issue summary: After a recent edge proxy (identity-proxy) rollout, some internal CLI users and a small fraction of Jenkins service jobs are failing to complete the Okta SSO assertion exchange. The client receives an interactive login loop: CLI prompts for browser SSO, browser completes login, but the CLI never enters an authenticated state and retries. Impact: ~12 devs and ~4 Jenkins jobs intermittently cannot perform authenticated operations (git pushes to internal mirrors, secret fetches) causing CI flakes. Root cause hypothesis centers on L7 header rewriting: identity-proxy changed ordering/duplication of X-Consumer and X-Auth-Assertion headers which downstream SSO-gateway mapping logic treats as different and sometimes ignores the intended assertion.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use internal CLI (redwood-cli v2.1.7) and run 'rw auth login --sso' behind corp VPN
2) Complete browser SSO flow when redirected to Okta, observe success on browser
3) Watch CLI: instead of receiving token it prints 'Waiting for assertion...' then restarts the flow
4) On a failing Jenkins job, observe repeated 401s when calling /internal/secrets with identical Okta assertion payloads in the request headers
logs: identity-proxy: INFO incoming request /auth/callback headers=(X-Consumer: svc-jenkins, X-Auth-Assertion: present)
sso-gateway: WARN ignored assertion header; found duplicate X-Auth-Assertion (order: X-Auth-Assertion, X-Consumer) -> mapping failed
cli-auth: ERROR assertion verification failed: header-mismatch (expected first header X-Auth-Assertion, got X-Consumer)
comments: 2025-02-18 09:14 Priya Kapoor (Support): Customer-facing impact limited to internal devs and CI; flagged to oncall. Collected repro steps and three example request traces.

2025-02-18 10:02 Ethan Chen (Oncall): Reproduced locally behind proxy; confirmed that swapping header order in a local proxy tests causes the sso-gateway to ignore the assertion. Forwarding to infra team owning identity-proxy.

2025-02-18 13:37 Marisol Vega (Infra): Recent edge config rolled yesterday included 'preserve-multiple-headers: false' which canonicalizes header order. Rolling back to previous config as a mitigant. Creating patch to normalize header merging rules in proxy.

2025-02-19 08:55 Security (Omar Haddad): Confirmed no evidence of assertion leakage in logs; all affected headers are internal and ephemeral. Recommend adding assertion integrity checks and telemetry.

2025-02-20 11:20 Ethan Chen (Assignee): Patch for identity-proxy header handling created (git ref: refs/changes/infra/identity-proxy/handle-multi-header-ordering). Need code review and deployment window. Temporary workaround documented for CLI users.
investigation_notes: Initial repro shows sso-gateway mapping uses first-occurring header instance for X-Auth-Assertion; proxy canonicalization changed which header appears first when multiple values present.
Only requests where both X-Consumer and X-Auth-Assertion are proxied in quick succession were affected — many requests never hit the codepath because clients send single headers.
Trace correlation: trace IDs 20250218-jnk-07, 20250218-dev-12 show identical assertion payloads but different header ordering; one accepted, one ignored.
Risk assessment: rollback of edge config reduces throughput for 2% of traffic but mitigates immediately. Longer-term fix in proxy is low risk.
Related patterns: Jenkins service jobs that use older http client libs append headers differently which exposed the ordering sensitivity.
resolution_notes: Mitigant: Rolled back identity-proxy config 'preserve-multiple-headers' to true at 2025-02-18 14:10; immediate reduction in errors reported by CI and dev callers.
Fix: Infra change to identity-proxy to normalize multi-header merge semantics and ensure X-Auth-Assertion is forwarded as a single canonical header (PR: refs/changes/infra/identity-proxy/1234).
Follow-up: sso-gateway to be hardened to accept assertion from any duplicate header position; ticket INT-516600 created to track that change.
Workaround for affected users: run 'rw auth login --sso --force-browser' or for service jobs ensure HTTP client upgraded to libs that do not duplicate headers; CI team notified with job-level patch.
Post-deploy monitoring: added a metric 'auth.assertion.ignored' and alert if rate > 1/min sustained.
sre_runbook_steps: 1) If new errors appear, rollback identity-proxy config 'preserve-multiple-headers' immediately.
2) Triage: gather trace IDs and sample raw headers from identity-proxy and sso-gateway for affected requests.
3) Apply hotfix patch to normalize header merging; target deploy window off-peak.
4) Notify security and CI teams once mitigation applied and monitor metrics for 24h.
